newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah rebounds on liquidity worries.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah rebounds on liquidity worries.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah rebounded against the dollar in late trading on Wednesday after the market switched focus from concerns about President's Suharto age to liquidity expectations, dealers said.
One U.S. bank dealer said offshore operators seemed to revise their early positions after they realised Suharto's comment about his age was not really fresh.
Dealers said Suharto had made similar comments before elections in past years.
Suharto said on Tuesday people who wished to see him stay in office for five more years should consider his age because he will be 77 next year when the president election is held.
The U.S. bank dealer said operators started to worry about Thursday's liquidity on market talk of a possible larger amount of maturing short-term papers (SBPUs).
"They sell outrights, reflected by declines in spot dollars and swaps, reversing earlier positions," he added.
Another said many players were too long on dollars and were forced to cut down in the wake of the liquidity uncertainty.
"We saw the money market being tightened sharply for tax payments at the fiscal year end. It could be tighter ahead of the new reserve rate," the U.S. bank dealer said.
Dealers said liquidity remained the main worry as operators prepared for a higher reserve rate effective on April 16.
Spot rupiah was at 2,398.00/98.25 at 0915 GMT against an opening of 2,398.25/99.00. Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,397.75/98.00 and 2,398.25/98.50, respectively.
The rupiah weakened briefly in early trading following offshore response on Suharto's comment about his age.
"I think he's being coy," Juwono Sudarsono, professor of political science at the University of Indonesia, said, adding that he did not think the comment should be taken seriously.
Dealers said the central bank also surprised the market by lowering the fixing rates on Wednesday.
The cental bank lowered its intervention band by one point to 2,394/2,586 and the conversion band to 2,394/2,442.
Tom/next swaps were at 0.27/0.33 and spot/next at 0.9/1.0.
The U.S. bank dealer said dollar selling in the afternoon was not a surprise because of the weekend factor.
He said players usually sold off to cover back on Thursday to enjoy some weekend premiums.
One-month swaps were at 10.50/11.00, two at 21.75/22.75, three at 33.5/34.5 and six at 68.75/70.00 points.
